_README: REGISTRY OF EVERY NUMBER THIS PROJECT STATES PUBLICLY.
Every figure that appears in README.md, MODEL.md, or any email to an
outside reader MUST be registered here, and `scripts/verify_claims.py`
must pass. `tests/test_claims_registry.py` enforces that in CI.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Every published error in this project's history had one
of three shapes, and none of them were caught by prose norms (REVIEWER.md
already said 're-derive, don't inherit' and it did not prevent any of
them):
(A) INCOMMENSURABLE COMPARISON -- two numbers compared that differ in
more than the one respect being claimed. The plain-vs-IR comparison
differed in BOTH the IR constraint and the tie-breaking rule. The
'25x tiebreak' claim compared a range over all tied optima against
a gain under one fixed rule.
(B) INHERITED NUMBER -- a figure established under method X reused under
method Y without re-derivation. 'Gain is always exactly 1' was true
of a first-hit search and false of the max-gain census. Size-effect
p-values were carried over from the tiebreak analysis.
(C) SCOPE OVERREACH -- evidence covering population P stated as a claim
about superset Q. 'The IR constraint never binds' was tested only at
the truthful profile. The determinacy denominator counted hospitals
that were already fully matched and so could not gain by
construction.
The three checks below are machine-executable versions of 'do not do that'.
SCHEMA, per claim:
id            unique slug
text          the sentence as a reader will see it
kind          'comparison' | 'measurement' | 'theorem'
scope         EXACTLY what population the evidence covers. Required.
unit          the unit of analysis for any count or inference
eligibility   which rows are admissible, and which are excluded and why
sources       data files the number is derived from. Must all exist.
arms          (comparison only) each arm's full config dict
varies        (comparison only) the ONLY keys allowed to differ
status        'verified' | 'retracted' | 'under_review'

claims.text: At 250 pairs the withholding rate goes from 1.00% to 7.67%, a gap of 6.7 points.
claims.scope: P=250 only; real Pansart2022 compatibility graphs; synthetic seeded hospital ownership; does not cover P=500 or chains/altruists.
claims.eligibility: All outcome-blind hospital checks that resolved in both arms. Zero skipped in either arm.
claims.blocker: The K=3 arm cannot be re-derived: results/samesolver_k3/summary.json was never written (the run was killed mid-P=500) and witnesses.jsonl was corrupted by a duplicate-launch race that truncated it while a second process held it open. The figure 23/300 survives only in a session log, which is not repo data. The K=2 arm (3/300) is intact. Re-run the K=3 arm, or cite the census-based comparison instead, which is derivable from committed rows.

claims.text: Imposing IR costs exactly 0 transplants at k=2 (645 instances) and 0.034% at k=3 (2,106 instances); never infeasible in 2,751 instances.
claims.scope: Truthful profiles only, on real Pansart2022 graphs. Says nothing about efficiency cost under misreports.
claims.eligibility: All instances where both the plain and IR optima were proven optimal.
claims.note: Compares OPTIMAL VALUES, which are tie-break independent. This is why it survives the tie-break confound that invalidated ir_reduces_withholding.
claims.blocker: No derivation written yet. The figures come from results/kidney_ir_sweep/efficiency.jsonl and are believed sound (they compare optimal values, which are tie-break independent), but until a derivation regenerates them they are not cleared.

claims.text: IR reduces the withholding rate from 10.8% to 3.8% (McNemar p = 0.0008).
claims.scope: P=250, k=3, paired on identical market and hospital.
claims.retraction: The arms differ in BOTH 'mechanism' and 'tiebreak', but only 'mechanism' was claimed to vary. Since manipulability is provably tie-break contingent at k=2 (MODEL.md 7.4b) and empirically so at k=3, the two effects are not separable in this design. The RATE MAGNITUDES are therefore unreliable. NOTE: this retraction is about the magnitudes only -- see ir_creates_manipulations, which re-tests the qualitative finding under a matched tie-break and largely confirms it.

claims.text: The IR constraint creates withholding opportunities that do not exist under the unconstrained mechanism: of 9 such cases, 7 survive a matched-tie-break control.
claims.scope: P=250, k=3, the 9 discordant cases where the paired run found a deviation under IR but not under plain. NOT a rate estimate over the full population; the denominator here is those 9 cases, not all hospitals.
claims.eligibility: The 9 IR-only discordant pairs from the paired run. Both arms use the SAME lexicographic tie-break; the control arm is the IR model with all standalone floors set to zero, which makes the constraint vacuous while holding the tie-break fixed.
claims.note: Mechanism: the standalone floor is computed over a hospital's TRUE pairs (witness/kidney_ir.py standalone() calls market.pairs_of), so withholding does NOT lower the floor. It lowers only the amount the mechanism can credit toward that fixed floor, which makes the constraint bite harder under a misreport than under truth. This is the opposite of an earlier stated explanation. The paired RATES cannot be attributed to the constraint alone; the 7-of-9 result comes from the matched-tie-break control, which is the only part of this claim that is asserted.

claims.text: At k=2, no misreport gives a hospital more than U_max. Proved in MODEL.md 7.3; corroborated on 324 verified deviations in the k=2 census.
claims.scope: Proved for all k=2 markets (MODEL.md 7.3). The 26,584 figure is corroboration on real+synthetic data, not the basis of the claim.
claims.eligibility: Deviations where both u_true_min and u_true_max were proven optimal, the realized truthful utility lay inside that range, and replay verification did not fail.
claims.challenge: The same measurement at k=3 returns 188 of 1,362, so the check is capable of detecting failures and the k=2 zero is not vacuous. The claim's basis is the proof, not this count.

claims.text: 0 of 94,655 determinate k=2 hospitals with room to gain, on the n=100 synthetic arm, have a profitable deviation.
claims.scope: Real benchmark plus one Erdos-Renyi generator at four parameter settings. NOT four independent generator families.
claims.eligibility: EXCLUDES hospitals already matching all their own pairs, which cannot gain by construction. Including them inflated an earlier version of this denominator to 490,147.
claims.challenge: Adversarial dense regimes (d=0.30, d=0.45) where 17-21% of INDETERMINATE hospitals do manipulate were run specifically to break this; determinacy held. Hospitals already matching all their own pairs are excluded, since they cannot gain by construction and would pad the denominator.
